learning_objectives.description: Distinguish between 2xx, 4xx, and 5xx response status categories.

content_blocks.content: HTTP is a request-response protocol in the client-server model. A transaction starts with a client submitting a request to the server, and the server returns a response describing the disposition of the request.
In this lesson, you will learn to explain GET and POST methods and distinguish between 2xx, 4xx, and 5xx response status categories.
A request identifies a method to classify the desired action to be performed on a resource.

The GET method requests a representation of a resource. The server should only retrieve data and not modify state. GET is preferred over POST for retrieving without making changes because it can be addressed through a URL, enabling bookmarking, sharing, and caching.
The POST method is used for actions where data is sent to the server, and the response contains an entity describing or containing the result of the action.
When a client sends a GET request for a customer resource, the request start line specifies method GET, URI /customer/123, and protocol version HTTP/1.1.
A response is sent to the client by the server, starting with a protocol version, a status code, and optionally a reason phrase.

Standard 2xx responses indicate successful HTTP requests. A 4xx status code is for situations in which an error seems to have been caused by the client. A 5xx status code indicates that the server is aware that it has encountered an error or is otherwise incapable of performing the request.

sections.title: Worked Examples of Requests and Responses

content_blocks.content: For a successful GET request, the server returns a 200 status code where the response contains an entity corresponding to the requested resource. For a POST request, the response contains an entity describing or containing the result of the action.
Apply your knowledge by categorizing various HTTP transactions based on methods and status codes.
Answer the following questions to check your understanding of HTTP methods and status categories.
Complete the final assessment questions to demonstrate your mastery of HTTP requests and responses.
You have reviewed how GET and POST methods function and how to distinguish between 2xx, 4xx, and 5xx response status categories.

claims.text: HTTP is a request–response protocol in the client–server model.
A request identifies a method to classify the desired action to be performed on a resource.
The server should only retrieve data; not modify state when handling GET.
A response is sent to the client by the server, and the start line consists of the protocol version, a status code and optionally a reason phrase.
A 4xx status code is for situations in which an error seems to have been caused by the client.
5xx status indicates that the server is aware that it has encountered an error or is otherwise incapable of performing the request.
Standard response for successful HTTP requests is 2xx.

activities.title: Analyze HTTP Transactions
activities.instructions: Examine a set of sample HTTP transaction logs. Identify whether each transaction uses a GET or POST method and categorize their return codes into 2xx, 4xx, or 5xx status categories. Analyze the following 6 sample transactions: 1. GET /index.html 200, 2. POST /submit 201, 3. GET /missing 404, 4. POST /update 400, 5. GET /error 500, 6. POST /fail 503.

assessments.prompt: The GET method is intended to modify the server's state.
assessments.explanation: GET requests should only retrieve data and not modify state.

assessments.prompt: Which status code category indicates an error caused by the client?
assessments.explanation: A 4xx status code is for situations where an error seems to have been caused by the client.

assessments.prompt: A client application attempts to fetch a user profile using a URL, but receives a 500-range status code back from the server. Based on this, how should you explain the outcome?
options: The server encountered an internal error or is incapable of performing the request.
The client submitted an invalid URL.
The client needs to send a POST method instead.
assessments.answer_key: The server encountered an internal error or is incapable of performing the request.
assessments.explanation: 5xx status codes indicate that the server is aware that it has encountered an error or is otherwise incapable of performing the request.

assessments.prompt: Why is GET preferred over POST when retrieving data without modifying state?
options: Because GET requests can be addressed through a URL, enabling bookmarking, sharing, and caching.
Because GET modifies the server state securely.
Because POST requests are always faster.
assessments.answer_key: Because GET requests can be addressed through a URL, enabling bookmarking, sharing, and caching.
assessments.explanation: GET is preferred for retrieving without making changes as it can be addressed through a URL, enabling bookmarking, sharing, and caching.
